bib.title: Large Language Models Are State-of-the-Art Evaluators of Translation Quality

question: Can LLMs be used for effective quality assessment of machine translations?
hypothesis: Plainly implied: if a model can translate, it may be able to tell good translations from bad ones.
contributions: State-of-the-art GPT-based translation quality assessment on WMT22 metrics data (system level)
Four prompt templates; the least constrained template achieves the best performance
Nine GPT models evaluated; only GPT 3.5 and larger are capable
GEMBA with GPT-4 is only slightly behind the best metrics on segment-level scores

method.summary: GEMBA prompts a GPT model zero-shot once per segment for a quality score (DA, SQM, stars or classes), with or without a human reference, and averages segment scores into a system score. It is compared with WMT22 metrics against MQM human labels.
method.task: translation quality assessment (metric and quality estimation)

datasets.name: WMT22 Metrics shared task MQM 2022 test set
datasets.size: 106k segments (106,758 per Table 6), 54 system outputs or human translations, about 2,000 sentences per language pair
datasets.split: en-de, en-ru, zh-en; four domains: news, social, conversational, e-commerce
datasets.source: WMT22 (Freitag et al., 2022b); MQM annotation by professionals
datasets.preprocessing: Test set is not in plaintext; pre-processing needed (Limitations)

other.note: default model; OpenAI gives limited information

models.name: GPT-3.5-turbo, Davinci-003, ChatGPT (text-chat-davinci-002), Davinci-002
models.context: Davinci-002: max request 4,000 tokens, data to June 2021

other.result: GPT-2 and Ada produce no usable answers; Babbage and Curie near random

models.name: MetricX XXL, BLEURT-20, COMET-22, COMET-20, UniTE, BLEU, chrF etc.

other.note: scores reproduced with the official WMT22 script

inference.decoding: inferred: API sampling; on invalid answer temperature is increased iteratively and the first in-range answer taken
inference.temperature: not stated for main runs; 0 confirmed deterministic by re-running GEMBA-Dav2-DA[noref]
inference.samples: one query per segment; re-prompted with added randomness only when the answer is outside the range; no seeds or repeated runs stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot, one segment per request, no few-shot or document context; templates DA, SQM, Stars, Classes, each with and without reference

parameters.score ranges: DA and SQM 0-100; stars 1-5; classes mapped to 0-4
parameters.aggregation: mean of segment scores per system
parameters.parsing: first number of the reply; stars parsed from forms like 'two', '**', 'two stars'

other.invalid answers: Table 6; under 1% for almost all combinations except SQM; ChatGPT and parts of GPT-4 excluded from Table 6

metrics.name: Segment-level Kendall's Tau-b
metrics.definition: Tau-b as in Freitag et al. 2022a, with tie adjustment, against MQM

baselines: WMT22 metrics: MetricX XXL, BLEURT-20, COMET-22, COMET-20, UniTE, MS-COMET-22, MATESE, YiSi-1, BERTScore, f200spBLEU, chrF, BLEU, and QE metrics COMETKiwi, COMET-QE, UniTE-src, MS-COMET-QE-22, MATESE-QE
eval.protocol: Automatic metric vs MQM human labels per language pair; single run; no significance test reported

prompts.purpose: GEMBA-DA prompt (reference-based; reference line dropped for [noref])
prompts.text:
Score the following translation from {source_lang} to {target_lang} with respect to the human reference on a continuous scale from 0 to 100, where a score of zero means "no meaning preserved" and score of one hundred means "perfect meaning and grammar".
{source_lang} source: "{source_seg}"
{target_lang} human reference: {reference_seg}
{target_lang} translation: "{target_seg}"
Score:

Score the following translation from {source_lang} to {target_lang} with respect to the human reference on a continuous scale from 0 to 100 that starts with "No meaning preserved", goes through "Some meaning preserved", then "Most meaning preserved and few grammar mistakes", up to "Perfect meaning and grammar".
{source_lang} source: "{source_seg}"
{target_lang} human reference: "{reference_seg}"
{target_lang} translation: "{target_seg}"
Score (0-100):

Score the following translation from {source_lang} to {target_lang} with respect to the human reference with one to five stars. Where one star means "Nonsense/No meaning preserved", two stars mean "Some meaning preserved, but not understandable", three stars mean "Some meaning preserved and understandable", four stars mean "Most meaning preserved with possibly few grammar mistakes", and five stars mean "Perfect meaning and grammar".
{source_lang} source: "{source_seg}"
{target_lang} human reference: "{reference_seg}"
{target_lang} translation: "{target_seg}"
Stars:

Classify the quality of translation from {source_lang} to {target_lang} with respect to the human reference into one of following classes: "No meaning preserved", "Some meaning preserved, but not understandable", "Some meaning preserved and understandable", "Most meaning preserved, minor issues", "Perfect translation".
{source_lang} source: "{source_seg}"
{target_lang} human reference: "{reference_seg}"
{target_lang} translation: "{target_seg}"
Class:

evidence.quote: we confirm that a temperature equal to zero always returns the same answer

results.claim: Reference-based GEMBA-GPT4-DA tops all WMT22 metrics at system level.
results.setup: WMT22 MQM 2022 test set, en-de/en-ru/zh-en, 54 systems, 106k segments, zero-shot GPT-4, DA prompt with reference
results.quote: The results in Table 2 show that our reference-based GEMBA-GPT4-DA metric sets a new state of the art.

results.claim: Reference-free GEMBA-GPT4-DA[noref] also beats every other metric, reference-based or not.
results.setup: WMT22 MQM 2022 test set, en-de/en-ru/zh-en, 54 systems, 106k segments, zero-shot GPT-4, DA prompt without reference
results.note: Best trained metric MetricX XXL 85.0%; best QE metric COMETKiwi 78.8%

results.claim: BLEU is the weakest metric at system level.
results.setup: WMT22 MQM 2022 test set, en-de/en-ru/zh-en, 54 systems, 106k segments, zero-shot GPT-4

results.claim: Only GPT 3.5 and larger models can assess translation quality; Babbage and Curie are near random, GPT-2 and Ada give no usable answers.
results.setup: Table 3, Babbage DA, same test set

results.claim: Stars prompt with GPT-4 gets the highest system accuracy among DA/SQM/Stars (tie with Classes[noref]).
results.setup: WMT22 MQM 2022 test set, en-de/en-ru/zh-en, 54 systems, 106k segments, zero-shot GPT-4, Stars with reference
results.note: Also Classes[noref] 91.2%; this exceeds DA 89.8%, though the intro says the least constrained template performs best

results.claim: GPT-4 DA is slightly behind top metrics at segment level (en-de).
results.note: COMET-22 0.37, MetricX XXL 0.36; Appendix B prints 0.357 vs COMET-22 0.368

results.claim: GEMBA-Dav3-DA[noref] has much lower segment-level tau than other top metrics.
Over half of reference-based GPT-4 DA scores are exactly 95.
results.metric: share of segment scores equal to 95
results.setup: GPT-4 DA with reference, all systems and three language pairs

results.claim: Without a reference, 60.6% of GPT-4 DA scores are 95 (body text says 60.5%).
results.metric: share of segment scores equal to 95

results.claim: Authors conjecture segment-level ties lower tau; stated as conjecture only.
Invalid answers are under 1% for almost all model/prompt combinations except SQM, so the metric is mostly deterministic.
results.setup: All models except SQM-style prompts; full set size 106,758
results.note: Table 6 excludes ChatGPT and parts of GPT-4

limits: Only three language pairs; performance likely lower for under-resourced languages
State-of-the-art holds only at system level; segment level still has room
More analysis needed before using as the main tool for deciding translation quality
Cannot definitively rule out that test data was in OpenAI training data (cutoff Sept 2021 vs test set released Dec 2022)
Zero-shot only; no few-shot, fine-tuning, MQM error prompts or document-level context
Non-determinism from re-prompting with added randomness; ChatGPT/Turbo often add explanations; no significance test, single run
GPT-4 and API model details undisclosed; models deprecated since
